label: early original-phase input of l/3/z/k/q after a prefix of mostly g,r,t,s,y,x,i,u,j,n,1,p
predicate: (phase == 0) & isin(in_tok, [tok("l"), tok("3"), tok("z"), tok("k"), tok("q")]) & (n_seen([tok("g"),tok("r"),tok("t"),tok("s"),tok("y"),tok("x"),tok("i"),tok("u"),tok("j"),tok("n"),tok("1"),tok("p")]) >= t-1) & (t>=2)
explanation: About 90% of activation mass falls in the original phase, peaking at t=3-4. It never fires at t=0 and almost never in the copy phase. The rest (about 9%) is at the <DEL> step. The input token is the main driver: l (9x lift, 36% of mass), 3, z, k and q, almost always on the first occurrence of that token. The largest activations are l or 3 at t=3-4 after a prefix made of tokens like g,r,t,s,y,x,i,u,j,n,1,p (first_tok and prev2_tok lifts of about 3x). Inputs such as v, o and b, and letters like a,h,w,c in the prefix, go with weak or no firing. Even in the best context, l/3/z fire on only a minority of steps, so the context dependence is graded and spread out, and a token-set predicate does not capture it. Dev F1 is about 0.39 and mass recall about 0.65.
